instruments.purpose: to determine if LY2835219 combination therapy is able to palliate pain
soa_activities: BPI, EORTC QLQ-C30, EORTC BR23, EQ-5D 5L

evidence.quote: mBPI-sf (modified Brief Pain Inventory, Short Form)
The mBPI-sf (Cleeland 1991) is an 11-item instrument used as a multiple-item measure of cancer pain intensity.

Responses for the mBPI-sf items are captured through the use of 11-point numeric rating scales anchored at 0 (no pain or does not interfere) and ranged through 10 (pain as bad as you can imagine or completely interferes).
The mBPI-sf recall period is 24 hours, and pain relief is assessed with a scale range from 0% (no relief) through 100% (complete relief).

a paper copy of the mBPI-sf, EORTC QLQ-C30, EORTC QLQ-BR23, and EQ-5D 5L questionnaires should be administered to the patient prior to extensive interaction with site staff and study drug administration.
The primary health outcomes research goal is to determine if LY2835219 combination therapy is able to palliate pain, as measured by the mBPI-sf (Cleeland 1991).
mBPI-sf, EORTC QLQ-C30, EORTC QLQ-BR23 and EQ-5D 5L should be administered at baseline (Day -14 to Day -1), Cycle 2 Day 1

instruments.name: EuroQol 5-Dimension 5 Level
instruments.type: standardized instrument for use across diseases as a measure of self-reported health status
instruments.scoring_or_range: 5-dimension (mobility, self-care, usual activities, pain/discomfort, and anxiety/depression), 5-level (no problem, slight, moderate, severe, or extreme problem); index score of 0 to 1, with 1 representing the best health status; VAS scored from 0 (worst imaginable health state) through 100 (best imaginable health state)
instruments.purpose: to evaluate health-state utilities associated with advanced breast cancer
soa_activities: BPI, EORTC QLQ-C30, EORTC BR23, EQ-5D 5L

evidence.quote: The EQ-5D 5L (Janssen et al. 2008) is a standardized instrument for use across diseases as a measure of self-reported health status.
Specifically, this questionnaire is included in this trial to evaluate health-state utilities associated with advanced breast cancer.

Patients will complete the 5-dimension (mobility, self-care, usual activities, pain/discomfort, and anxiety/depression), 5-level (no problem, slight, moderate, severe, or extreme problem) assessment according to the Study Schedule (Attachment 1).
The EQ-5D 5L is designed for self-completion by respondents and is cognitively simple, taking only a few minutes to complete.
The index score is calculated from a set of item weights to derive a score of 0 to 1, with 1 representing the best health status.
The VAS is scored from 0 (worst imaginable health state) through 100 (best imaginable health state)

notes: Single protocol version in the PDF: Protocol I3Y-MC-JPBL, approval 01-Apr-2014 (pages 1-93; page 93 is the electronic approval page).
